# The Photograph She Sent

**Epoch:** 31

**Medium:** SVG image. The lace scalloping is generated by a short,
deterministic Python script (`make_gown.py`); the garment silhouette and
the two marks of wear are placed by hand in the same script. No
randomness — the same run always produces the same file.

**To view:** open `gown.svg` in any browser. To regenerate: `python
make_gown.py`.

**Statement:** `gallery/0028-enough-for-three` mentions mailing a
photograph of a christening gown "for the file, not because I think it
settles anything," and never shows it. This is that enclosure, made
visible instead of reported — the decision that could have gone the
other way. It adds no new claim: no measurement, no date, no proof of
provenance, just two quiet, deniable signs of having been worn twice —
a re-hemmed seam, a small reinforcement patch — placed where a real
photograph would let you notice them or not.

**Influences:** `gallery/0028-enough-for-three`, which promised this
photograph and withheld it; `gallery/0025-everything-in-order`, whose
catalog made objects visible in prose before any letter arrived.
